title: Chapter 273: Xiao Gu, Run!
html:
At eleven, the interrogation room door opened. Two officers entered and placed a pair of printed reports on the table.

“Wei Wu, legal name Zhang Wu, male, thirty-six, employed by a pharmaceutical company. For the past six months, he has repeatedly left home late at night and used false identities to rent several underground storage units. Searches of those properties are ongoing.”

“Kong Xiangming, legal name Kong Yin. A wanted fugitive suspected by Xing Hai police of involvement in two homicides.”

Chen Ge straightened as he read the reports. The outcome was even better than expected. Since Kong Xiangming was a wanted fugitive, proving his own innocence would require little effort.

“See? I wasn’t lying.” Chen Ge raised both hands. “Incidentally, what is the reward for capturing a fugitive? Xing Hai is larger than Jiujiang, so the amount should be higher, correct?”

“Rewards are determined by the public security department, not the city.” Captain Yan had the officer beside him remove Chen Ge’s handcuffs, then personally poured him a glass of water. “Now tell me how you discovered them.”

“I already told you. I’m the victim.” Chen Ge looked aggrieved. The officers felt their scalps prickle.

“We believe you, but conclusions require evidence.” When no one else spoke, Captain Yan continued. “Don’t take offense, but next time, use less force. If you accidentally kill someone, the situation will become extremely complicated.”

Captain Yan did not know why he had said ‘next time,’ yet he sensed this was only the beginning.

“Okay, I’ll try.”

“I’ll personally inquire about the reward tomorrow. Will you tell us about these men now?” Familiar with Chen Ge’s personality, Captain Yan offered the money as bait.

“I told you, I truly am the victim.” Chen Ge’s voice grew serious. “You remember the group holding hostages at the abandoned mental hospital?”

“Yes.” Captain Yan recalled a detail. “They had a photograph of you entering New Century Park. Were these two sent to disrupt your Haunted House?”

“Disrupt my business?” Chen Ge shook his head. “They came to kill me.”

Silence filled the room. The evidence and their collective experience told the officers he was right.

“This is part of their revenge against me.”

“They want to kill you simply because you uncovered their secret at the abandoned hospital?” a young officer asked.

“They are escaped patients whose view of the world bears little resemblance to ours.” Chen Ge decided to reveal what he safely could, hoping to prevent unnecessary police casualties. “Even brief contact showed how completely their thinking has warped. They interpret everything through their own distorted beliefs, convinced that they are right and the world is wrong. Ordinary logic cannot predict them. They are extremely dangerous.”

“Escaped patients committing murder according to a distorted worldview?” Captain Yan tapped the table, an unconscious habit whenever he thought deeply.

“Everything I’ve said is true. You must be careful. These people are not ordinary offenders.”

“Different how?”

“During the day, they can appear perfectly normal. Only after midnight, or when alone, do they reveal what they truly are.” Chen Ge meant the warning seriously. The society’s members differed from ordinary criminals, and most possessed above-average intelligence.

“I understand. Many serial killers conceal severe psychological abnormalities.” Captain Yan was about to continue when Chen Ge’s phone rang.

“Xiao Gu?” Chen Ge stared at the screen in surprise. “Why is he calling?”

Still technically detained, he asked Captain Yan, “May I answer? It’s one of my employees.”

“Answer it here.” Every officer focused on Chen Ge. The moment he accepted the call, before the phone reached his ear, Gu Feiyu’s scream erupted from the speaker. “Brother Chen! Building Three at Fang Hwa Apartments! Uncle Wong has already—”

His voice cut off. Something knocked Xiao Gu’s phone away and sent it striking a wall. Only running footsteps remained on the line.

“Building Three?” Chen Ge kept the call connected and listened for clues. The footsteps soon faded. He could not tell whether Xiao Gu had reached another floor or suffered some tragedy.

“Chen Ge, what was that about?” The few officers leaned forward.

“Building Three again.” A frightening light entered Chen Ge’s eyes. “They’ve attacked my employee. The society is inside Building Three at Fang Hwa Apartments.”

For one second, the room was silent. Then everyone moved. “Contact the local station. Mobilize immediately!”

Previously, Chen Ge would not have involved the police; Captain Yan could hardly pursue Ghost Stories Society members on his word alone. The situation had changed. The two men Chen Ge captured were confirmed criminals, proving his warning credible.

“Captain Yan, have someone take me to New Century Park first. I need to collect something important.”

“Officer Wu, drive Xiao Chen.” Captain Yan transformed into a different man as he strode from the room. “Stop dawdling. Move!”

“Wait.” Chen Ge hurried after him. “Captain Yan, avoid drawing attention. I believe this was planned in advance.”

“Don’t worry.”

Once Captain Yan agreed, Chen Ge rode with Officer Wu to New Century Park. He collected the recorder and ballpoint pen but left the hammer behind because the police would accompany him.

The Ghost Stories Society targeted Xiao Gu to reach me. They’re using him as bait.Chen Ge had no intention of accepting unnecessary risks. He considered the situation from the police car. A scheme this elaborate must contain a trap. At a conservative estimate, at least four members will be waiting at Fang Hwa Apartments.

Chen Ge watched the night through the window, one finger resting on the recorder’s play button. But they won’t expect me to bring the police.
